AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND/PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) have been recently adopted in many fields of cardiovascular medicine and in interventional cardiology. Using CFD analysis we compared the use of different PCI procedures, with and without the utilization of a proximal optimization technique (POT), on a complex coronary artery bifurcation.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS/MATERIALS
AbstractText.content: For the analysis, we considered a hypothetic model of a left anterior descending artery-diagonal Medina 1,1,1 bifurcation type with a diameter of the proximal main branch (MB) and the side branch (SB) set at 3.5mm and 2.5mm, respectively. The bifurcation angle has been set to 50°. For the stent simulation, we reconstructed a third-generation, ultra-thin strut everolimus-eluting stent (ORSIRO stent, Biotronik IC, Bulack, Switzerland).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The Nano-crush and the modified T techniques seem able to restore the most physiologic fluid dynamic profile. Conversely, the DK-crush and the culotte demonstrated an intermediate and worst effect, respectively. The addition of a final POT resulted favorably for both Nano-crush and reverse modified T techniques, whereas a neutral and lack of significant effects have been observed for the DK-crush and culotte technique, respectively.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Different double-stenting techniques (DST) have a different impact on coronary flow physiology. Both Nano-crush and modified T techniques achieved the most physiologic profile. The addition of a final POT appears to be a favourable step for both Nano-crush and modified T.
